description: This file defines the Translate class within the Goteo project's model layer, responsible for managing user translations of different content types such as projects, calls, and nodes. It includes methods for retrieving, saving, removing, and managing translation permissions and statuses, as well as fetching available contents for translation.

classes.name: Translate
classes.description: Model class for handling user translations, including retrieval, validation, storage, deletion, marking as ready, and permission checks for translating various content types.

methods.name: get
methods.description: Retrieves the type of an item based on its ID, returning 'project', 'call', 'node', or false if not uniquely identified.

methods.name: getMine
methods.description: Fetches all translations of a specific type associated with a user.

methods.name: getMyProjects
methods.description: Shortcut for retrieving user project translations.

methods.name: getMyCalls
methods.description: Shortcut for retrieving user call translations.

methods.name: getMyNodes
methods.description: Shortcut for retrieving user node translations.

methods.name: getAvailables
methods.description: Returns a list of available items for translation based on type, node, and current item.

methods.name: validate
methods.description: Validates the translate object, checking for required fields and valid types.

methods.name: save
methods.description: Persists the translation record, creating or updating an entry in the database.

methods.name: remove
methods.description: Removes a translation association for a user.

methods.name: unready
methods.description: Reopens a translation, marking it as not ready.

methods.name: translators
methods.description: Lists users who have been assigned a specific translation item.

methods.name: is_legal
methods.description: Checks if a given user has permission to perform actions on a specific translation item.

methods.name: getLangs
methods.description: Retrieves translation languages enabled for a user.
